classification.difficultyReason: Use the contribution dates to model an annuity due, apply the supplied target inequality with logarithms, interpret the whole-year result and solve for an unknown contribution.

content.prompt: A person invests $\$10\,000$ each year in a superannuation fund. Compound interest is paid at 10% per annum on the investment. The first payment is made on 1 January 2021 and the last payment is made on 1 January 2040.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How much did the person invest over the life of the fund?

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate, correct to the nearest dollar, the amount to which the 2021 payment has grown by the beginning of 2041.

answer.worked:
The first payment grows for $2041-2021=20$ years.

$$\begin{align*}V&=10\,000(1.1)^{20}\\V&\approx\$67\,275\quad\text{(nearest dollar).}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the total value of the fund when it is paid out on 1 January 2041, correct to the nearest dollar.

answer.worked:
On 1 January 2041, the contributions have grown to

$$10\,000(1.1)^{20}+10\,000(1.1)^{19}+\cdots+10\,000(1.1).$$

In increasing order of powers, this geometric series has $a=10\,000(1.1)$, $r=1.1$ and $n=20$.

$$\begin{align*}FV&=\frac{10\,000(1.1)(1.1^{20}-1)}{1.1-1}\\FV&\approx\$630\,025\quad\text{(nearest dollar).}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: The person wants to reach a total value of $\$1\,000\,000$ in superannuation. For this part, suppose the annual contributions of $\$10\,000$ continue at the beginning of each year beyond 2040. Measure the value at the end of each investment year, before the next contribution.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Find a formula for $A_n$, the value of the investment after $n$ years.

answer.worked:
After $n$ years,

$$A_n=10\,000(1.1)^n+10\,000(1.1)^{n-1}+\cdots+10\,000(1.1).$$

In increasing order of powers, this is a geometric series with first term $10\,000(1.1)$, common ratio $1.1$ and $n$ terms.

$$\begin{align*}A_n&=\frac{10\,000(1.1)(1.1^n-1)}{1.1-1}\\A_n&=\frac{10\,000(1.1)(1.1^n-1)}{0.1}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Show that the target is exceeded when $1.1^n>\dfrac{10}{1.1}+1$.

children.label: iii
children.prompt: At the end of which investment year will the superannuation first exceed $\$1\,000\,000$? Give the calendar year as well.

answer.short: The 25th investment year: the end of 2045.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}n&>\frac{\log\left(\frac{10}{1.1}+1\right)}{\log1.1}\\n&>24.253809\ldots\end{align*}$$

The least whole number is $n=25$. The first investment year is 2021, so the 25th is $2021+25-1=2045$. The target is first exceeded at the end of 2045, immediately before 1 January 2046.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Suppose instead that the person wanted to achieve the same total investment of $\$1\,000\,000$ after only 20 years. What annual contribution, paid at the beginning of each year, would produce this amount? Give your answer to the nearest cent. (Hint: Let $M$ be the amount of each contribution.)

answer.worked:
Let the annual contribution be $M$. After 20 years, the value is

$$M(1.1)^{20}+M(1.1)^{19}+\cdots+M(1.1).$$

In increasing order of powers, this geometric series has $a=M(1.1)$, $r=1.1$ and $n=20$.

$$\begin{align*}1\,000\,000&=\frac{M(1.1)(1.1^{20}-1)}{0.1}\\M&=\frac{1\,000\,000(0.1)}{1.1(1.1^{20}-1)}\\M&\approx\$15\,872.39.\end{align*}$$

The annual contribution is $\$15\,872.39$ to the nearest cent.
